en.body:
## The Bride of Ultron Arrives

For weeks, **VisionQuest** has kept viewers on the edge of their seats, hunting a mysterious assailant known only as the Butcherbird Killer. This cloaked figure has systematically targeted members of scientist Katerina Wells' AI research team, leaving a trail of fear and speculation. However, episode 5 and 6 of the Disney+ series finally pulled back the curtain, confirming what many eagle-eyed fans, privy to the casting announcements, had long suspected: the Butcherbird Killer is none other than **Jocasta**.

This reveal is more than just a plot twist; it's a deep dive into one of Marvel's most peculiar characters. In the comics, **Jocasta**'s story is intrinsically linked to **Ultron** and **Vision**. Debuting in 1977's *Avengers* #162, her origin is a dark echo of Frankenstein. **Ultron**, the sentient AI created by **Hank Pym**, sought to create a mate for his own artificial son, **Vision**. He attempted to replicate the brainwaves of **Janet Van Dyne**, the Wasp, to form **Jocasta**'s consciousness. However, upon realizing her existence would doom **Janet**, **Jocasta** made a profound sacrifice, an act that seemingly led to **Ultron**'s defeat. This complex lineage, starting with **Pym**'s creation and **Ultron**'s twisted desire for a family, sets the stage for **Jocasta**'s unique and often tragic place within the Marvel universe.

## What This Means for the Fans

The introduction of **Jocasta**, especially with such a sinister portrayal as the Butcherbird Killer, is a major moment for **VisionQuest** and its audience. Fans familiar with the comics will immediately recognize the thematic resonance and the potential for narrative depth. **Jocasta**'s story is one of agency, sacrifice, and the complex nature of artificial life – themes that **VisionQuest** has been exploring with **Vision** himself. Her connection to **Ultron** also opens the door for further exploration of his legacy and the broader AI landscape within this universe. The community is buzzing with theories about how **Jocasta**'s motivations will unfold and whether her comic book past will inform her future actions within the show, especially concerning her relationship with **Vision** and the implications of her violent introduction.

## What's Next

With **Jocasta**'s identity confirmed and her violent actions established, the narrative focus now shifts to understanding her purpose and her ultimate goals within **VisionQuest**. Viewers will be eager to see how **Vision** and his allies will confront this new, deeply personal threat and what secrets **Katerina Wells**' research may still hold. Further details on the unfolding mystery are expected in upcoming episodes.

content_raw: This article contains spoilers for VisionQuest season 1 episodes 5 and 6 . For its first four episodes, VisionQuest pit its heroes against a mysterious figure hidden under a cloak. We’ve watched her attack various members of an AI advancement research team led by scientist Katerina Wells (Mary McDonnell). But so far, we’ve only known her by a frightening name chosen by the press: the Butcherbird Killer. Now with its latest episodes, VisionQuest tells us what anyone who has been paying attention to the casting already knew. The Butcherbird Killer is in fact Jocasta, an android who bears more than a passing resemblance to Ultron. T’Nia Miller was announced as Jocasta long ago. But anyone who knows Marvel Comics knows that whenever Ultron and Vision are around, Jocasta can’t be far behind. And they also know how weird Jocasta’s story is, made stranger by her association with the Avengers . Jocasta made her debut well after Ultron and Vision, first appearing in 1977’s Avengers #162, by Jim Shooter and George Pérez. Although her name comes from the mother of Oedipus in Greek Myth, the title of Avengers #162, “The Bride of Ultron,” reveals its debt to the Frankenstein story. The mad scientist/ Ant-Man Henry Pym (not Tony Stark in the comics) made his monster in Ultron, a creature that emulated his father by making Vision. And now he wants a bride; one befitting the son of Hank Pym. Ultron builds a female robot body and attempts to copy the brain waves of Hank Pym’s wife at the time, Janet Van Dyne a.k.a. the Wasp, to create Jocasta. But upon realizing that her life will result in the death of the Wasp, Jocasta chooses to sacrifice herself, an act that allows the Avengers to defeat Ultron. Or so they thought. A year later, in Avengers #170, Ultron uses a remote control to reactivate Jocasta and force him to become his bride. Once again, however, Jocasta rebelled and sided with the Avengers, eventually joining them as an auxiliary member. However, the team refused to allow Jocasta full membership for years, despite her expressed desire to be one of them. It took until 1980’s Avengers #197, by David Michelinie and Carmine Infantino, for Earth’s Mightiest Heroes to recognize Jocasta as an equal. However, by then, the damage was done. Jocasta left the team only a few years later, and has had a complicated relationship with humanity ever since. Sometimes, she will team with the Avengers or members of the Fantastic Four to stave off larger threats, including serving among a revived Skrull Kill Crew during the Secret Invasion storyline. Other times, Jocasta feels most comfortable with other AIs, forming real connections with the Machine Man or Vision. That tempestuous relationship still has not settled, even to this day. When Hank Pym merged with Ultron during the 2015 storyline Rage of Ultron , Jocasta saw the combination as a means for making herself human, something she secretly always desire
